stem: A dashboard used by hundreds of concurrent viewers must load instantly and only needs to reflect data as of last night's scheduled refresh, not the current moment.

choices.text: Import the dataset into Amazon QuickSight and hold it in SPICE memory storage
Configure the QuickSight dataset to query the source directly on every load
Run the same Athena query again for every dashboard view instead of caching it
Schedule an AWS Glue DataBrew job that writes a CSV extract to S3 each morning

rationale: Importing the dataset into QuickSight's SPICE in-memory engine avoids re-querying the source on every interaction, giving hundreds of concurrent viewers a fast, cached dashboard that matches the nightly-refresh freshness the requirement accepts. Querying the source directly on every load re-runs the query for every viewer, trading away the fast, cached performance the scenario wants for freshness the scenario does not need. Re-running the same Athena query for every view has the same repeated-query cost and no dashboard layer for viewers to interact with. Glue DataBrew is a visual data-preparation tool for cleaning and normalizing data, so a scheduled job that writes a CSV extract to S3 produces a prepared file, not an interactive dashboard hundreds of people can load and explore.
